title: The essence of calculus (3Blue1Brown)
summary: Grant introduces the Essence of Calculus series, aiming to make learners feel they could have invented calculus themselves through visual reasoning. He derives the area of a circle by slicing it into thin concentric rings, approximating each as a rectangle of area 2πr·dr, and showing that the sum of these approaches the area of a triangle under the graph of 2πr, giving πR². He generalizes this to show that many problems built from sums of small quantities reduce to finding the area under a graph, introducing the integral as an area function such as the area under x². By examining how that area changes with a small nudge dx, he shows that dA/dx approximates the height of the graph, introducing the derivative. He closes by explaining that this inverse relationship between integrals and derivatives is the fundamental theorem of calculus.

topics.name: Circle area via concentric rings
topics.summary: The area of a circle is approximated by slicing it into thin rings, each unwrapped into a rectangle of area 2πr·dr, with the approximation improving as dr shrinks.

topics.name: Sums as area under a graph
topics.summary: The ring rectangles are arranged under the graph of 2πr, and as dr shrinks their total area approaches the triangle under the graph, giving exactly πR².

topics.name: Integrals as area functions
topics.summary: Many problems made of sums of small quantities, like distance from velocity, reduce to finding the area under a graph, leading to the idea of an integral function A(x) for the area under x².

topics.name: Derivatives as rates of change
topics.summary: Nudging x by dx changes the area by about x²·dx, so the ratio dA/dx approaches the graph's height, which introduces the derivative as a measure of a function's sensitivity to small input changes.

topics.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
topics.summary: The derivative of the area-under-a-graph function gives back the original function, showing that integrals and derivatives are inverses of each other.
